record_only.description: The paper frames the initial retinal condition as macular edema secondary to branch retinal vein occlusion and the acute event as acute angle-closure glaucoma / acute angle closure after intravitreal bevacizumab injection.
The patient received intravitreal bevacizumab 1.25 mg/0.05 mL in the right eye using a 30-gauge needle; a third injection was given after recurrence of macular edema.
At emergency presentation, the patient was treated with 300 mL of 20% intravenous mannitol, followed by right-eye laser iridotomy; prophylactic left-eye laser iridotomy was performed after 3 days.
One hour after mannitol, intraocular pressure was 14 mmHg in the right eye and 16 mmHg in the left eye, and right corneal epithelial edema decreased.

One month after laser iridotomy, intraocular pressures were 13 mmHg right and 15 mmHg left, iridotomy sites were patent, right-eye visual acuity was 0.7, and no glaucomatous visual field defect was evident.
Ocular biometry one month after laser iridotomy measured anterior chamber depths of 2.42 mm right and 2.12 mm left and axial lengths of 22.64 mm right and 22.50 mm left.
The discussion emphasizes hyperopic eyes, narrow angle, post-injection intraocular pressure elevation, and blocked reflux at the injection site as possible contributors.
